instruction: Patient reports persistent fatigue and frequent urination over the past month. (Case 1)
context: A 56-year-old male with a 10-year history of type 2 diabetes presents complaining of worsening fatigue and polyuria for the past four weeks. He is currently on metformin 1000 mg twice daily and glargine insulin at night. The patient admits to inconsistent glucose monitoring and has been struggling with dietary compliance. His last HbA1c, taken six months ago, was 8.4%. He denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or weight loss but admits to mild blurry vision in the evenings. He works as a taxi driver, often skips meals, and consumes energy drinks to stay awake. His blood pressure is 142/88 mmHg, and BMI is 31 kg/m².
response: The patient’s symptoms and history suggest suboptimal glycemic control, likely due to dietary inconsistency and irregular insulin administration. Fatigue and polyuria indicate possible hyperglycemia. Recommend ordering fasting glucose, postprandial glucose, and repeat HbA1c testing. Reinforce the importance of regular monitoring and structured meal planning. Adjust insulin regimen as necessary after reviewing glucose trends. Advise limiting sugary beverages and energy drinks. Consider screening for diabetic nephropathy and retinopathy given the duration of diabetes. Schedule follow-up in four weeks to reassess symptoms and lab results.

instruction: Patient seeks advice about planning pregnancy while having type 1 diabetes. (Case 3)
context: A 29-year-old female with type 1 diabetes diagnosed since adolescence presents for preconception counseling. She is on a basal-bolus insulin regimen and uses continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Her HbA1c last month was 6.8%. She has no known diabetes-related complications. The patient expresses anxiety about managing glucose during pregnancy and possible effects on fetal health. She follows a healthy diet and engages in moderate exercise three times a week. No history of hypertension or renal disease. She is currently taking folic acid and oral contraceptives but plans to discontinue them soon to conceive.
response: This patient is appropriately seeking preconception guidance. Optimal glycemic control before conception reduces the risk of fetal malformations and maternal complications. Counsel her to maintain HbA1c <6.5% prior to pregnancy. Continue CGM use and frequent glucose monitoring. Ensure she is on preconception folic acid supplementation (at least 400–800 µg daily). Review and discontinue any contraindicated medications. Once pregnant, insulin requirements will change, necessitating close monitoring and multidisciplinary care involving an endocrinologist and obstetrician. Reinforce dietary counseling, weight management, and early prenatal care.

instruction: Patient presents with swelling of the feet and reduced urine output for the past two weeks. (Case 1)

instruction: Patient found unconscious at home with a glucometer reading of 42 mg/dL. (Case 2)

Educate the patient and caregiver on recognizing early hypoglycemia and keeping glucose gel or tablets readily available. Consider reducing basal insulin dosage or using a CGM with low‑glucose alerts. Assess for any contributing renal dysfunction or medication interactions that may prolong insulin action. Follow‑up within one week is advised.
